newsitem.title: HONG KONG: WEEK AHEAD - Hong Kong stocks glued to FOMC.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - Hong Kong stocks glued to FOMC.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are expected to take their lead from the Federal Reserve's meeting this week, sustaining recent gains if interest rates remain steady but suffering a setback if rates move higher, analysts said.

"I think the local stock market will take clues from Wall Street. On the one hand, the market will see whether the Fed will raise rates and the local market will also observe how sensitive the U.S. stock market is," said Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities.

"If the rise is a quarter point, I don't think it will have a big impact on the market. It may go down a bit but it will bounce back very quickly. If it is more than 25 basis points, the immediate reaction will be down 200 or 300 points."
The Hang Seng index hit a year high at 11,645.35 points last Tuesday before spending the rest of the week treading water ahead of this Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
The blue chip index rose 223.32 points, or 1.96 percent, over the week after closing Friday's session on a gain of 5.68 points at 11,592.36.
Andrew Fernow, director of research at Vickers Ballas, said there was a strong possibility of a rate hike.
"We believe there could be a near term negative reaction to that event," he said, adding that the Hang Seng could drop 200 to 300 points.
But Alan Hutcheson, director of research at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, disagreed. "To my mind there is still no clear trend on rates," he said.

Hutcheson said it would be hard for the market to make much headway after its recent rally. "I think the market by and large has had its rally already. I don't see it going substantially above where it reached last week."
The Hang Seng index has risen 566.77 points over the past two weeks.

"We had a recent rally because people expected the Fed to leave rates unchanged. So even if they do, we will see selling on the good news," said Ricky Tam, senior research analyst at Delta Asia Securities.
"If they raise rates, that will shock the whole market. I think the market will drop all the way to 11,000," he said.
However, Peter Lai, associate director at OCBC Securities, remained optimistic on the market and said an interest rate hike of less than 50 basis points had already been discounted.
"I think the market will try to test 11,700. If it breaks through, it will try to go to 12,000," he said.
Kwong agreed that a new year high could be reached next week. "If there is no rate hike the market will expect interest rates to remain stable for at least one or two months."
"If there is sufficient funds participation may be the index could search higher," he said, adding that he expected a range of 11,400 to 11,800 points for the Hang Seng next week.
